content.prompt: Hana works from 8:30 am to 4 pm on Monday and from 9 am to 2:30 pm on Tuesday. Her hourly rate is \$26.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the number of hours Hana works on Monday.

answer.worked:
From 8:30 am to 4 pm is 7 hours 30 minutes.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Hours}&=7.5\text{ hours}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Calculate her total pay for Monday and Tuesday.

answer.worked:
From 9 am to 2:30 pm is $5.5$ hours on Tuesday.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total hours}&=7.5+5.5\\&=13\text{ hours}\\\text{Total Pay}&=\$26/\text{hour}\times13\text{ hours}\\&=\$338\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Find the number of hours from 10:30 am to 4 pm.

answer.worked:
From 10:30 am to 12 pm is $1.5$ hours, and from 12 pm to 4 pm is $4$ hours.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Hours}&=1.5+4\\&=5.5\text{ hours}\end{align*}$$

payloads.replacement:
- These conversions are close estimates.
  A non-leap year has 365 days, but 52 weeks have only 364 days.
- A common misconception is that four weeks equal a month.
  Four weeks is 28 days, and only February in a non-leap year has 28 days.

- **Wages** are hourly payments for work.
- Employers usually pay wages weekly or fortnightly.
- When Mr Ding worked at McDonalds, he earned a wage of \$12 per hour.
  His fortnightly pay depended on his hours worked.
- Wages vary with the hours you work. More hours earn more, while fewer shifts or unpaid leave reduce your pay.

- **Overtime** is work beyond the agreed number of hours, which depends on the job.
- **Penalty rates** are higher wages paid for:
  - Overtime
  - Weekend work
  - Night shifts
  - Public holidays

- **Commission** is pay calculated as a percentage of the value of a salesperson's sales.
- Some salespeople earn a base salary called a **retainer**, plus commission.
Sometimes someone earning a commission is also paid a [[retainer|24]], which is a fixed amount not affected by sales.

- A **salary** is a fixed amount of pay per year, often written as per annum (p.a.).
- Employers divide a salary into weekly, fortnightly or monthly payments.
- When Mr Ding began teaching, he was paid \$72 000 p.a.
  Every fortnight, he was paid $\frac{1}{26}$ of \$72 000.
- Salaried workers often have paid leave.
- Some may also earn overtime, but this is rare.

- **Bonuses** are one-off rewards for good work, usually paid at the end of the year.
- **Allowances** are extra pay for difficult or dangerous working conditions, leadership positions, or work-related expenses, e.g. uniforms and travel.
Holiday pay includes leave loading, so it is [[117.5|17]]% of 4 weeks’ pay.

sourceAtom.visibleSubtitle: Calculate pay using equivalent normal hours

inlines.text: Noah earns $28 an hour and works 30 normal hours, 6 hours at time-and-a-half and 2 hours at double time in a week.
b) Ella works the same hours in a week and earns $1376 in total. What is her hourly rate?

inlines.latex: \begin{align*}\text{Equivalent normal hours}&=\text{Normal hours}+(\text{Time-and-a-half hours}\times1.5)\\&\quad+(\text{Double time hours}\times2)\\&=30+(6\times1.5)+(2\times2)\\&=43\text{ h}\end{align*}
\begin{align*}\text{a) Total pay}&=\text{Normal pay per hour}\times\text{Equivalent normal hours}\\&=28\times43\\&=\$1204\end{align*}
